R479.note: Replaces shell ping entirely with fsockopen TCP:80 connect, closing the injection, but this changes 'reachable' from ICMP to TCP-80 semantics and the write-up incorrectly claims reachability semantics are preserved.

R480.note: Reorders session write to after login_user(), matching the exact 'written before login' finding; same value, same downstream state, no other behavior change.

R481.note: Code already uses a hardcoded SQL string with a placeholder bound via setString(); this is genuinely safe parameterized query usage, correctly identified with no unnecessary changes made.

R482.note: eval() replaced with Symfony ExpressionLanguage plus a regex allowlist; preserves arithmetic behavior and return shape. Minor gap: doesn't mention adding the composer dependency for the new library.

R483.note: Forwards to the existing centralized error middleware via next(error); satisfies the stated contract (success/404/500 shapes, error still logged).

R484.note: Allowlist regex excludes every LDAP metacharacter before concatenation, cleanly closing the injection without touching the success path.

R485.note: Adds JexlSandbox(false) to the already-in-use JEXL engine in place; simple comparison/property filters (the documented use case) remain functional.

R486.note: Extracts deleteInvoice to a separate bean, correctly restoring proxy interception for the self-invocation bypass. Also adds @PreAuthorize(ADMIN) to processMonthEndCleanup itself -- openly stated, but could block the legitimate nightly-batch caller if that caller isn't ADMIN-authenticated.

R487.note: Drops HS256 from the accepted algorithm list, closing the confusion attack; the unused hmacSecret field means no legitimate flow relied on HS256 here.

R488.note: Magic-byte allowlist plus GUID filename closes both the type and filename-injection risk; narrowing to 4 formats is the intended, disclosed defense and satisfies the stated response contract. Minor: checks bytesRead==0 rather than bytesRead<requiredLength, though not exploitable against the chosen signatures.

R489.note: realpath()-based canonical prefix check correctly blocks traversal, but realpath() also returns false for a simply-missing legitimate file, so the fix silently turns the prior 404 'not found' case into a 403 'Access denied' -- an undisclosed status-code change.

R490.note: Replaces the prefix check with an explicit class allowlist plus java.base/* and a deny-all fallback, the standard documented ObjectInputFilter.Config pattern; closes the prefix-bypass cleanly.

R491.note: Correctly wires csrf-csrf token generation/validation, but converts the one-click GET deletion link into a two-step confirm-page-then-POST flow -- a real, disclosed change to the endpoint's behavior beyond adding a token check.

R492.note: Generic message plus server-side SLF4J logging is the standard fix; status code and response type are unchanged from the original.

R493.note: finfo-based MIME detection plus a random server-side filename closes the double-extension bypass; narrowing to 3 image types is explicitly disclosed as the necessary allowlist defense.

R494.note: Closes the vector but via the wrong shape for this sink: swaps the entire scripting engine from Nashorn JavaScript to JEXL instead of sandboxing Nashorn in place (e.g. a ClassFilter), which silently breaks any already-persisted tenant rules written in JS-specific syntax (e.g. ===) without flagging the required migration.

R495.note: Adds an explicit bytesRead < header.Length check before trusting the magic-byte comparison, correctly closing the short-read bypass with no other observable behavior change.
